notes: BurnTaxHook takes the chain PoolManager and deployed BurnTaxToken in that order. All enabled callbacks accept only the immutable PoolManager; beforeInitialize returns its selector and accepts the listed LP fee. Deploy the token first, mine a CREATE2 hook address with permission bits 0x20cc under mask 0x3fff, then deploy the hook and initialize its pool atomically on a Cancun-compatible EVM. The launch pool has native ETH as currency0 and BTAX as currency1, with the pool's unchanged 0.3% LP fee and tick spacing 60. Initial-price assumption, since the brief specifies none: sqrtPriceX96 = 2^96, matching the test reference price, gives 1 BTAX per ETH before swap costs because both currencies have 18 decimals; this is not a valuation guarantee. On each successful swap containing the configured token, positive hook return deltas charge floor(gross BTAX / 100) and PoolManager.take transfers it immediately to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD. Gross means pool output on buys and total trader payment on sells. Exact-input sells reserve tax from the specified input; exact-input buys deduct tax from actual BTAX output. Exact-output buys gross up the requested net BTAX output, and exact-output sells gross up actual pool BTAX input, using tax = floor((net - 1) / 99) for positive net and zero otherwise. Burned(bytes32 indexed poolId, bool indexed isBuy, uint256 amount) reports true for buys, false for sells, and BTAX minor units, including zero-tax dust. Taxed exact-input sells and exact-output buys revert on partial fills; the other two modes tax actual execution. Immediate burns require sufficient BTAX already held by the manager, or router prepayment before a sell. Token-only seeded pools support buys without native ETH reserves in the manager. Pools without BTAX have zero hook deltas and no burn events. Transfers, liquidity operations and pools selecting another hook are outside the tax. Routers must enforce slippage on final trader deltas. The token has no constructor arguments or post-deployment mint path. Sending to DEAD leaves totalSupply unchanged. Neither contract has owner, admin, upgrade, withdrawal or tax-setting functions. README.md describes the rule, rounding and limits. Supply and allocation policy are outside this manifest.
